2. Mesoscopic observations and screening🔗

Home / Section index / Main §6

We compare finitely many mesoscopic observations of the periodic Riesz diffusion with Gaussian vectors, uniformly in the observation times. The error determines admissible shrinking scales and yields a stationary limit after a diverging rescaled waiting time.

Throughout, the particle system is assumed to satisfy the strong-solution and filtration hypotheses below.

Proposition 6.1 is developed through the comparison estimate, the admissible scale range and the stationary limit. The low-frequency behavior gives the accompanying remark.

Objects · Comparison · Scales · Stationary window · Low frequency · Paper-to-Lean map

2.1. Objects and hypotheses🔗

Fix an integer 𝖽≥2\mathsf{d}\ge 2d≥2, 0≤𝗌<𝖽/20\le \mathsf{s}<\mathsf{d}/20≤s<d/2, and q=𝖽−𝗌q=\mathsf{d}-\mathsf{s}q=d−s. Fix a finite number ppp of real, smooth, compactly supported tests ϕa\phi_aϕa​ on Euclidean 𝖽\mathsf{d}d-space, and a center x0x_0x0​. For ℓ>0\ell>0ℓ>0 the periodized test is

ϕℓ(x)=ℓ−𝖽/2∑z∈ℤ𝖽ϕ ⁣(ℓ−1(rep⁡(x)−x0+z)).\phi_\ell(x)=\ell^{-\mathsf{d}/2}\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^{\mathsf{d}}}\phi\!\left(\ell^{-1}(\operatorname{rep}(x)-x_0+z)\right).ϕℓ​(x)=ℓ−d/2z∈Zd∑​ϕ(ℓ−1(rep(x)−x0​+z)).(6.1)

The observation is ZN,ℓt(ϕ)=N(μNt−dx)(ϕℓ)Z_{N,\ell}^t(\phi)=\sqrt N(\mu_N^t-\mathrm dx)(\phi_\ell)ZN,ℓt​(ϕ)=N​(μNt​−dx)(ϕℓ​), with normalized Haar measure dx\mathrm dxdx. Observations are taken at physical times ℓ2−qta\ell^{2-q}t_aℓ2−qta​, ta≥0t_a\ge0ta​≥0.

Let N≥2N\ge2N≥2 and β>0\beta>0β>0. Assume a collision-free strong solution of the periodic Riesz particle system with zero external potential on every finite time interval, started from product Haar law. The driving Brownian motions are jointly independent of the initial positions. Require a Brownian filtration relative to which the solution is adapted and progressively measurable. The local stochastic hypotheses below specify the lift, time-integrable drift, initial condition, measurable time slices and almost-sure continuity.

Lean proof. HRS.screening_comparison_proof proves the comparison. The source checks that its type matches HRS.screening_comparison, the earlier declaration in Sec6.lean whose proof is admitted with sorry. Archived verification records cover the _proof theorem and this type check in nanoda and Lean’s default kernel.

Proof. For ℓ≤1\ell\le1ℓ≤1, combine the commutator estimate with the small-scale probabilistic and Gaussian comparisons. The same commutator constants give nonnegativity of the corrected energy. Enlarge the comparison constant to at least 222. For ℓ>1\ell>1ℓ>1, use d3≤2d_3\le2d3​≤2 and the ℓ\ellℓ term in the error. The small-scale argument transports the test functions and combines the two comparison errors.

2.4. Stationary limit🔗

Fix 0<κ<κmax⁡0<\kappa<\kappa_{\max}0<κ<κmax​. Take N=n+2N=n+2N=n+2, ℓn=(n+2)−κ\ell_n=(n+2)^{-\kappa}ℓn​=(n+2)−κ, positive βn\beta_nβn​ with βnℓnq→b>0\beta_n\ell_n^q\to b>0βn​ℓnq​→b>0, and a sequence of supplied stochastic systems satisfying the hypotheses above. For any nonnegative un→∞u_n\to\inftyun​→∞ and fixed nonnegative lags tat_ata​, the smooth distance of order 3 between observations at physical times ℓn2−q(un+ta)\ell_n^{2-q}(u_n+t_a)ℓn2−q​(un​+ta​) and the centered Gaussian with mesoStatCovMatrix d s b t φ tends to zero.

For all sufficiently large particle counts, the scaled temperature lies in [b/2,2b][b/2,2b][b/2,2b]. Apply the comparison estimate and the vanishing-error result. The covariance entries of the comparison Gaussian converge to the stationary entries; the Gaussian comparison bound therefore gives convergence in smooth distance. The triangle inequality completes the proof for the fixed tests and lag times.

The proved declaration is HRS.screening_stationary_limit_proof. Its type is checked against the original HRS.screening_stationary_limit, whose proof is admitted with sorry.

Normalization and conventions🔗

Write 𝖼𝖽,𝗌\mathsf{c}_{\mathsf{d},\mathsf{s}}cd,s​ for the Riesz normalization

𝖼𝖽,𝗌={2𝖽−1π𝖽/2Γ(𝖽/2),𝗌=0,2𝖽−𝗌π𝖽/2Γ((𝖽−𝗌)/2)/Γ(𝗌/2),𝗌≠0.\mathsf{c}_{\mathsf{d},\mathsf{s}}=\begin{cases}2^{\mathsf{d}-1}\pi^{\mathsf{d}/2}\Gamma(\mathsf{d}/2),&\mathsf{s}=0,\\ 2^{\mathsf{d}-\mathsf{s}}\pi^{\mathsf{d}/2}\Gamma((\mathsf{d}-\mathsf{s})/2)/\Gamma(\mathsf{s}/2),&\mathsf{s}\ne0.\end{cases}cd,s​={2d−1πd/2Γ(d/2),2d−sπd/2Γ((d−s)/2)/Γ(s/2),​s=0,s=0.​(6.8)

For the definitions, 𝖽∈ℕ\mathsf{d}\in\mathbb Nd∈N and the displayed real parameters are unrestricted. Scalar operations have their total real meanings: zero inverse is zero, and real powers use the total real-power convention. A sum or Bochner integral is assigned zero when it is nonsummable or nonintegrable, respectively.

Stochastic hypotheses.

On a probability space (Ω,P)(\Omega,P)(Ω,P), the initial configuration has product Haar law. The N𝖽N\mathsf{d}Nd real coordinates of WWW are independent standard Brownian motions, jointly independent of the initial configuration. The torus-valued process XXX has measurable time slices, almost surely continuous paths, and the prescribed initial condition.

For each T≥0T\ge0T≥0, there is a lift YYY of XXX to (ℝ𝖽)N(\mathbb R^{\mathsf{d}})^N(Rd)N such that, almost surely, its drift is integrable and

Yi(t)=Yi(0)−1N∫0t∑j≠i∇𝗀(Xi(v)−Xj(v)) dv+2/β [Wi(t)−Wi(0)](0≤t≤T).Y_i(t)=Y_i(0)-\frac1N\int_0^t\sum_{j\ne i}\nabla\mathsf{g}(X_i(v)-X_j(v))\,\mathrm dv+\sqrt{2/\beta}\,[W_i(t)-W_i(0)]\qquad(0\le t\le T).Yi​(t)=Yi​(0)−N1​∫0t​j=i∑​∇g(Xi​(v)−Xj​(v))dv+2/β​[Wi​(t)−Wi​(0)](0≤t≤T).(6.32)

The particles are almost surely distinct throughout each [0,T][0,T][0,T]. There is a Brownian filtration carrying a version of WWW equal in all coordinates and times almost surely, relative to which XXX is adapted and progressively measurable; for real times use Xmax⁡(t,0)X_{\max(t,0)}Xmax(t,0)​. The kernel 𝗀\mathsf{g}g is the periodic Riesz kernel and the external potential is zero.
